name: Natural selection as an evolutionary mechanism
summary: Darwin, and later Wallace independently, explained how living things adapt: inherited variations that help survival and reproduction become more common over generations.
description: Heritable variation and differential survival/reproduction provide a natural mechanism of adaptive change; Darwin’s recorded formulation and Wallace’s later independent account are distinguished.
tier_reason: The explanatory mechanism underlies subsequent evolutionary biology, ecology and population research across generations, independently of a particular surviving notebook.
why: Darwin, sorting observations from the Beagle voyage, read Malthus on population pressure in 1838; Wallace reached the same idea while collecting in the Malay Archipelago.
